title: QuantLab: narrow-beam burst harness for FP16/INT8/INT4 perf vs quality
creator: Juniper Hayes
description: Build a new focused benchmarking harness (QuantLab narrow-beam) to evaluate FP16 / INT8 / INT4 quant profiles under bursty arrival patterns and long-tail prompt mixes. The harness will measure tokens/sec, per-request p95 latencies, tail variance, and semantic quality degradation. Core goal: provide deterministic regression detection for production rollouts when switching quant profiles or kernel sets, while surfacing operational knobs (batching, kv-cache warmup, sequence bucketing) that materially change tail behavior.
acceptance_criteria: Harness can replay 3 synthetic traffic profiles (steady, bursty, long-tail spike) with configurable qps and concurrency
Collect tokens/sec and p50/p90/p95/p99 per route and per-quant-profile and export to Grafana/Console

Quality checks: semantic similarity and structured pass/fail on held-out prompt set run across FP16, INT8, INT4 with thresholds: BERTScore >= baseline-0.015 or embedding-cosine >= 0.98 per prompt group
Regression detection: EWMA-based alarm and bootstrap significance test implemented; false positive rate under control on historical baseline traces
KV cache scenarios included: cold start, prefix-shared, and hot cache; results annotated in exported reports
End-to-end reproducible artifact (script + config) checked into github.com/redwood-inference/quantlab with CI job and a linking Grafana dashboard
test_plan: Create three synthetic traffic generators: steady-plateau (10 q/s), bursty-peaks (1s bursts to 200 q/s), and long-tail sessions (90% short, 10% >1024 tokens)
Run each generator against model variants: fp16-baseline, int8-perchannel, int4-group with 5 seeds each to capture stochasticity
Collect latency histograms, tokens/sec, kernel utilization, and memory pressure metrics for each run
Run quality evals: BERTScore, ROUGE-L, and structured API conformance checks on 2k held-out prompts; compute per-prompt delta vs FP16 baseline
Apply bootstrap confidence intervals to mean quality delta and run Mann-Whitney U as robustness check
Validate regression alarm behavior by injecting a known perf regression (sleep in kernel) and confirming EWMA alarm triggers within configured window
progress_updates: 2025-02-14: Kickoff meeting with runtime, infra, and evals teams. Aligned on three traffic templates and quality metrics.
2025-02-18: Prototype traffic generator implemented (nodejs/gRPC) and preliminary steady-state runs against fp16 baseline; tokens/sec measurement stable.
2025-02-22: Added KV cache modes and sequence-length buckets. Observed INT4 high variance in cold-warm transitions; captured detailed logs for kernel team.
2025-02-26: Implemented EWMA detector and bootstrap pipeline. Running multi-seed runs on ci/quantlab-runner. First false-positive tuning iteration reduced rate from 12% to 3%.
2025-03-02: Integrated results export to grafana and created dashboard skeleton (PR open). Preparing long-tail 2k prompt quality run next.
2025-03-03: Scheduled design review with PM and SRE to finalize alarm thresholds and rollback playbook.
decisions: Use BERTScore (cased) + embedding cosine as primary quality checks because token-level perplexity was insufficiently correlated with downstream API conformance
Adopt EWMA on p95 as primary perf alarm for regression detection; pair with bootstrap significance tests on quality deltas for release gating
Limit INT4 testing to controlled groups (group-quant) and require explicit canary traffic before global rollouts
Report both cold-cache and steady-cache numbers; do not aggregate them into a single number in Console to avoid masking regressions

notes: This ticket purposefully uses narrow-beam traffic templates to expose tail behaviors that broad benchmarks miss. Aim is to keep runs small and fast so engineers can iterate quickly while still producing statistically meaningful signals. Ensure all outputs are human-readable and machine-consumable for rollout automation.
